whatItIs: The Windows paging file. Windows uses it as extra memory when your RAM fills up, so it is often several GB.
consequenceIfDeleted: Windows will not let you delete it while running. Its size is managed in Windows settings (Advanced system settings, Performance, Virtual memory); removing it can cause crashes and out-of-memory errors.

whatItIs: A small Windows file that holds the memory of suspended Store apps.
consequenceIfDeleted: Windows keeps it locked. Store apps rely on it to resume quickly.

whatItIs: The hibernation file. Windows saves your memory here for Hibernate and Fast Startup, so its size is a share of your RAM.
consequenceIfDeleted: You cannot delete it directly. Turning hibernation off removes it and frees the space, but you lose Hibernate and Fast Startup.

howToClean.text: Turn hibernation off from an administrator terminal. Turn it back on any time with "powercfg /hibernate on".

whatItIs: A tiny log Windows writes when it records a crash or a stack dump.
consequenceIfDeleted: Nothing. Windows may recreate it.

whatItIs: A full memory dump Windows saved after a crash (blue screen). It can be many GB.
consequenceIfDeleted: You lose the crash report, which only helps when diagnosing that crash. Windows is unaffected.

howToClean.text: Disk Cleanup or Storage settings can remove system error memory dump files for you.

whatItIs: A cache of picture thumbnails that Windows Explorer keeps in a folder.
consequenceIfDeleted: Windows recreates it the next time the folder is viewed with thumbnails. Thumbnails may load slowly once.

whatItIs: A cache of thumbnails or icons that Windows Explorer shows.
consequenceIfDeleted: Windows rebuilds it automatically. Icons and thumbnails may look blank for a moment.

whatItIs: A hidden settings file that gives a folder a custom icon or a translated display name.
consequenceIfDeleted: The folder loses its custom icon or display name. Nothing else changes.

whatItIs: Part of a Windows user profile: it stores that account's registry settings (desktop, apps and preferences).
consequenceIfDeleted: The account loses its settings or fails to sign in. Windows usually locks it while the user is signed in.

whatItIs: The Windows Search index: a database of what is on your PC so searches are fast. It can reach many GB.
consequenceIfDeleted: Windows rebuilds it, but search is slow and incomplete while it re-indexes, which can use a lot of CPU and disk for hours.

whatItIs: The virtual disk of a Linux distribution that runs under WSL. Everything in that distro, including your files there, lives inside it.
consequenceIfDeleted: You permanently lose that Linux distribution and every file you stored in it. Export it first with "wsl --export".

whatItIs: The virtual disk where Docker Desktop keeps its images, containers and volumes.
consequenceIfDeleted: You lose every Docker image, container and volume. Docker re-downloads images, but volume data is gone.

howToClean.text: Remove unused Docker data from inside Docker instead of deleting the disk.

whatItIs: An SSH private key: your secret login for servers and services such as GitHub.
consequenceIfDeleted: You lose access to every server or account that trusts this key, unless you have a copy. It cannot be regenerated to match.

whatItIs: A cryptocurrency wallet file. It holds the keys to coins.
consequenceIfDeleted: You can permanently lose the coins it controls if you have no backup of the keys.

whatItIs: A temporary file that a program made while it worked.
consequenceIfDeleted: Nothing, once that program is closed. If a program is still using it, Windows will not let you delete it.

whatItIs: A log file: a text record of what a program or Windows did.
consequenceIfDeleted: You lose the history, which only matters when diagnosing a problem. The program starts a new log.

whatItIs: A crash dump: a snapshot of memory saved after a program or Windows crashed.
createdBy: Windows Error Reporting or the crashed program
consequenceIfDeleted: You lose the crash report, which only helps diagnose that crash. Nothing stops working.

whatItIs: An event trace log that Windows or a program wrote for diagnostics.
consequenceIfDeleted: Only the diagnostic history is lost. Windows writes new traces as needed.

whatItIs: An unfinished download that a browser or app left behind.
createdBy: A web browser or download manager
consequenceIfDeleted: You lose the partial download. If it was still wanted, you have to download it again.

whatItIs: Python bytecode: a speed-up cache Python builds from your .py files.
consequenceIfDeleted: Python recreates it the next time the program runs.

whatItIs: A folder-view file made by macOS that ended up on this PC.
consequenceIfDeleted: Nothing on Windows. It only held how the folder looked on a Mac.

whatItIs: A shortcut: a small file that points to a program, file or website.
consequenceIfDeleted: Only the shortcut goes. The thing it points to is untouched.

whatItIs: A backup copy of another file, kept by a program or by someone before a change.
consequenceIfDeleted: It may be the only copy of an earlier version. Check that the current file is good first.

whatItIs: A program component: a driver or library that Windows or an app loads.
consequenceIfDeleted: Programs or Windows can stop working or fail to start. Uninstall the program from Settings instead.

whatItIs: A program or installer, or a script that runs commands.
consequenceIfDeleted: If it is an installed program, it stops working. If it is an installer you downloaded, you can fetch it again, unless it is no longer available.

whatItIs: A disc or system image: a whole disc, installer or Windows setup packed in one file.
consequenceIfDeleted: A downloaded image can usually be downloaded again. One you made yourself is lost for good.

whatItIs: A compressed archive: several files packed into one.
createdBy: You, or someone who sent or published it
consequenceIfDeleted: You lose everything packed inside unless it exists elsewhere. Check what is in it before deleting.

whatItIs: A virtual hard disk: the whole disk of a virtual machine in one file.
createdBy: A virtual machine program (Hyper-V, VirtualBox, VMware, WSL)
consequenceIfDeleted: You lose that virtual machine and everything stored inside it.

whatItIs: An Outlook data file. It can hold your emails, contacts and calendar.
consequenceIfDeleted: You can lose emails, contacts and calendar entries that are not stored anywhere else.

whatItIs: An Outlook offline cache of a mailbox that lives on a server.
consequenceIfDeleted: Outlook downloads it again from the server, which can take a while for a big mailbox. Anything not yet synced is lost.

whatItIs: A database file. Programs keep their saved data in files like this.
consequenceIfDeleted: The program can lose its saved data or stop working. Which one depends on where the file lives.

whatItIs: A settings or data file that a program reads.
consequenceIfDeleted: The program may reset its settings or fail to start.

whatItIs: A key, certificate or password vault. It proves who you are, or stores your passwords.
createdBy: You, a service or a password manager
consequenceIfDeleted: You can permanently lose access to accounts or secrets. Many of these cannot be recreated.

whatItIs: A document: text, a spreadsheet, a presentation or a PDF.
createdBy: You, or someone who sent it to you
consequenceIfDeleted: You permanently lose it unless you have a copy. If your cloud storage syncs this folder, the deletion spreads there too.

whatItIs: A picture or photo.
createdBy: You, a camera, or a program that saved it
consequenceIfDeleted: You permanently lose it unless you have a copy. Photos are often irreplaceable.

whatItIs: A video.
createdBy: You, a camera, or something you downloaded or recorded
consequenceIfDeleted: You permanently lose it unless you have a copy. Videos are usually the biggest files on a PC, so check it first.

whatItIs: An audio file: music, a recording or a sound.
createdBy: You, or something you downloaded or recorded
consequenceIfDeleted: You permanently lose it unless you have a copy.

whatItIs: Source code or a script.
consequenceIfDeleted: You lose that code unless it is in version control (such as Git) or backed up.
